newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zaire ex-envoy back to France for trial.
newsitem.headline: Zaire ex-envoy back to France for trial.

text.p: Zaire's former ambassador to France returned to Paris on Saturday, saying he wanted to put his conscience at peace by standing trial over the deaths of two boys in a traffic accident in the Riviera resort of Menton.
Ramazani Baya landed at Paris' Charles de Gaulle airport on a flight from Kinshasa. It was not immediately clear whether he had been summoned by an investigating magistrate.
"I am coming back of my own free will after resigning from my duties as ambassador in order to answer for the accident... which caused the death of two children," he told reporters at he airport.
As relatives of the two boys demanded that he be brought to justice, the French government had asked Zaire to lift his diplomatic immunity shielding him from justice.
"I have decided of my own free will to resign, which the head of state has accepted, and which opens the way to a trial," Baya told TF1 television before leaving Zaire.
"As a father myself, I realise the tragedy and the (parents') suffering. I know that only the trial they are demanding could bring them some comfort," Baya told TF1.
"I will not be in peace until this this judgment has been passed," he said.
Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko said last week he had relieved Baya of his functions and diplomatic immunity so that he could stand trial for last November's accident.

French police have said Baya, who was on his way to visit Mobutu at the Zairean leader's Riviera villa, was driving at more than twice the legal speed limit when he hit Raphael Lenoir, 13, and Ronald Lehartel, 12, on a pedestrian crossing.
He could face up to three years in jail if convicted of manslaughter.

Relatives of the boys and thousands of residents of Menton have demonstrated at the scene of the accident and had threatened to protest outside Mobutu's mansion at nearby Roquebrune-Cap-Martin if Baya was not brought to trial.
Patrick Lenoir, the father of one of the dead boys, welcomed Baya's statement. "I think he realised our tragedy and he sounded sincere," he said.
Mobutu, who is a close ally of France in Africa, is resting at his Riviera villa after cancer treatment.
